newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HISTORY PROVES PEDIGREE OF BRAZIL AND ITALY. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HISTORY PROVES PEDIGREE OF BRAZIL AND ITALY. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: A glance at the record books is enough to prove that Brazil and Italy share a very special soccer rivalry and that their meeting in the Tournoi de France on Saturday (corrects from Sunday) could produce something special.

Of their five previous competitive meetings two have been in World Cup Finals, one in a World Cup semifinal and one in a World Cup third-place playoff. Two of the five are generally regarded as being among the best games ever played.

A recent book, which suggests the 100 greatest matches of all time, puts Italy's 3-2 win over Brazil in the second round of the 1982 World Cup in Barcelona as the third greatest match ever played. Number four on the list is the 1970 World Cup Final in which Brazil, Pele, Gerson, Rivelino et al beat Italy 4-1.
Different people will place those matches higher or lower on the scale but there is no doubt that they deserve to rank among soccer's greatest encounters.
For different reasons, their most recent meeting, the 1994 World Cup Final at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, will always be remembered too.
That match has a special place in soccer folklore not because it was a great match but because of the drama of the penalty shootout after the teams finished 0-0 after extra time.

Although it was a totally unsatisfactory way for the World Cup final to de decided, the image of Roberto Baggio sinking forlornly to his knees after missing the penalty that gave Brazil a 3-2 penalty shootout victory will never be forgotten by those who saw it.
Italy first met Brazil in the World Cup semifinals in 1938 when they beat them 2-1 in Marseille on their way to retaining the trophy.

It took Brazil 32 years to avenge that defeat but on June 21 1970 in the Aztec Stadium in Mexico they did it and were crowned world champions after playing with style, flair, skill and a sparkle that has never been bettered.

Italy came to the match just four days after a draining 4-3 semifinal win over West Germany -- and hardly made an impression against Brazil in a match at which permanent possession of the Jules Rimet trophy was at stake after both had won it twice previously.

Pele, playing in his final World Cup match, put Brazil ahead after 18 minutes rising high above the defence to power home Rivelino's cross and become the second man, after Vava, to score in two World cup finals.
Careless play in the Brazilian defence allowed Boninsegna to level for Italy before half-time but in the second half Brazil utterly destroyed the Italians.

Gerson scored with a brilliant left-footed shot to make it 2-1 after 66 minutes and five minutes later supplied the pass for Jairzinho to make it 3-1 and become the only player to score in every game in a World Cup finals.

And then after 86 minutes came one of the best goals ever scored. A long ball out of defence found Jairzinho on the wing. One touch found Pele on the edge of the box. He did not even need to look to know that Carlos Alberto was rushing down the wing and laid off the most exquisite of passes for his skipper who, without breaking stride, smashed it past Albertosi to score Brazil's fourth. It is debatable whether any goal has been shown on television more often.
Twelve years later there was a very different outcome from another classic.
While 107,000 watched the 1970 Final, only 44,000 were crammed into Espanyol's Sarria stadium in Barcelona to see a second round match the organisers had not expected to take place.

The reason it happened so early in the competition was because Italy, playing poorly, finished only second in their opening-round group and so had to play Brazil, who had played outstandingly to win their section, in their second-round group.
Brazil had won all three first round matches and defeated Argentina 3-1 in their first second-round match. They needed only a draw against the Italians to make the semifinals.
But then they came across Paolo Rossi. Rossi had made a poor start to the World Cup and not scored a goal. But by the end of that afternoon he was a national hero.
His first goal came within five minutes of the start when he headed Italy in front. Italy were on their way not only to knocking out Brazil but winning the whole tournament.

Within seven minutes Socrates had equalised but then Rossi scored again after intercepting a loose back pass. Still the match ebbed and flowed and Brazil came storming back with Falcao blasting an extraordinary goal to make it 2-2 with 20 minutes left.

If the game had finished level, Brazil would have gone through -- but it did not. With 15 minutes to go, Rossi turned in a shot from Marco Tardelli to complete his hat-trick and give Italy the lead for the third time. Skipper Dino Zoff made an amazing save from Cerezo's header in the final minute and Italy won.

They went on to beat Poland in the semifinal and West Germany in the final with Rossi ending the tournament top scorer with six goals. They still talk about that match in Rome. They have not forgotten it in Rio either.
